items.title: Reliable attached-client baseline
acceptance: Run pinned tmux and freshly built zz with isolated homes/config roots and short sockets; record binary hashes, source revision and dirty state, OS, TERM, shell and dimensions.

Retain attach, input, daemon and outer-screen diagnostics on every geometry-fixture timeout, proven by a driven failure. The geometry-report timeout recorded on macOS on 2026-09-09 is handed to TUI-013 for reproduction or explanation there (clause split 2026-09-09 by fabrico's deferral; reversible).

Produce a repeatable baseline at 80x24, 100x24 and 120x24 with all measured differences and fixture limitations retained, including the waived wide-terminal columns. This package proves fixture reliability, not runtime parity.
items.evidence_note: MEASURED 2026-09-09 on alienware (CachyOS, 16 cores, Linux) from worktree /home/demfabris/dev/zz-tui-lane at 576b6b745821856d9c00b3a62d6a1982fd8571e1, clean apart from this attempt's own files. zz built fresh in that worktree; pinned tmux d77c9dc6, sha256 df2cafcb212e8b69677dd57c2bd0c3bb59592eaf385d974ec0124526d6b63ee5, tmux -V next-3.8. TERM=xterm-ghostty, bash 5.3.15, LANG=en_US.UTF-8 with LC_TIME=pt_BR.UTF-8. environment.txt records both binaries' sha256, the worktree revision and dirty state, the OS, TERM, shell, locale and the sizes each fixture drives. The zz hash identifies the artifact but does not attest it: a cargo debug build of zz is not bit-reproducible on this box, and the cycle-18 reviewer rebuilt -p zz at this same worktree path from the same source and got a different hash, and a third from another worktree. Provenance rests on reproduction instead, which is stronger: that independently built zz reproduced these fixture results and TUI-002's 195 capture files byte for byte. The pin's hash verifies exactly. GEOMETRY: compat/tui-pane-geometry.sh exits 0 SIX times out of six, 4 to 5 seconds a run against its own 10 second bound - three runs of the fixture as it stands at origin/main and three of the fixture after this attempt's timeout-diagnostics change. 80x24 both 80 columns, 100x24 both 100, rows 23 on both sides at all three sizes. CLAUSE 2 IS NOT SATISFIED BY THIS ATTEMPT: the recorded macOS geometry-report timeout is neither reproduced nor explained here, and it stays open. The stale-pre-fix-binary story this attempt first argued is REFUTED by the campaign's own registry, inside the very gap that was cited as its authority. tui.client-input-backpressure (closed 2026-09-07 at 0bed7fe7) does cite compat/tui-pane-geometry.sh among its evidence and does record the cause exactly, crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs flush_output blocking the main event loop; but its resolution rules that stall out as the cause of a macOS geometry expiry, verbatim: "It also exited 0 at origin/main 012b4dcc before the fix, so the macbook expiry the cycle-17 gate recorded is not this stall reproducing there: that script drives the pane through the CLI's send-keys, not through the client's stdin, and its inner clients run inside an outer pinned tmux that reads their output continuously, so no backpressure ever builds. What remains on the macbook is unexplained and belongs to whoever next runs the tool there." Two refutations, either one sufficient. EMPIRICAL: 012b4dcc is 2026-09-07T10:45:51-03:00, after the fixture reached its current shape at 314c55e0 (00:15:42) and before the fix at 0bed7fe7 (13:31:08), which is exactly the window a stale binary would have to come from, and the registry records this fixture exiting 0 there - so a pre-fix binary running this fixture is measured as PASSING. MECHANISM, and it is platform-independent: the fixture's inner clients run inside an outer pinned tmux that drains their output continuously, so the backpressure flush_output stalled on never builds in this fixture at all; if no backpressure builds, the macOS pty write buffer's size is irrelevant and the pre-fix stall cannot fire on any platform, which the earlier draft's pty-buffer hedge does not reach. WHAT SURVIVES of that explanation is two measurements, neither of which reaches the macOS record: the fixture and the runtime are sound at this revision (six exit-0 runs, the measure() wait nowhere near its bound), and the named backpressure cause is measurably absent here (compat/run.sh --strict-geometry smoke/tui-client-input-backpressure exits 0 with 0 divergences). CLOSING CLAUSE 2 NEEDS a run of compat/tui-pane-geometry.sh on macOS with an attested binary, retaining the timeout dump this attempt added if the geometry-report wait fires. The timed-out binary's own revision is unrecoverable: the shared checkout's target/debug/zz was rebuilt on this box at 18:25 on 2026-09-09, so its hash says nothing about the record. FIXTURE CHANGE, in zone: a bounded wait that runs out now copies out, before the scratch tree is removed, which wait fired, both outer screens via capture-pane -p -e -S -, both servers' client and pane lists, the zz daemon's stdout and stderr, and each attached client's own stderr teed out of its pane; the fixture also pins ZZ_LOG_DIR into its scratch tree and scrubs XDG_STATE_HOME so it can no longer write into the box's real state directory. Proved by sabotage: file_has_two_fields was made to demand three fields, the fixture exited 2 with the record's own text "zz geometry report did not happen within 10 seconds" and left fourteen files, retained under timeout-diagnostics/; the edit was reverted and runs 4 to 6 are the unsabotaged fixture. That dump is what a macOS run would need to retain, and it is the part of this attempt clause 2 can still use. CLAUSE 3 RECORD, for TUI-004: at 120x24 the pin hands its pane 120 columns and zz hands its pane 91, rows 23 on both. The 29 column difference is the sidebar's 28 plus its 1 column border, the same arithmetic as AUTO_HIDE_COLUMNS = 80 + 28 + 1 = 109 in crates/zz-tui/src/sidebar.rs. Recorded, not asserted: tui.sidebar-auto-hide is a standing decision and TUI-004 owns changing it. FIXTURE LIMITATION AND A NEW DIVERGENCE: compat/status-row.sh exits 1 on this box, 2 of 11 comparisons, and the cause is the locale rather than the status row. Only the two steps that still carry the default status-right differ, and only in %b: the pin prints "09-set-26" and zz prints "09-Sep-26". The pin expands %b through libc strftime(3), which honours LC_TIME=pt_BR.UTF-8; zz expands it in crates/zz-mux/src/formats.rs:4707 format_datetime through chrono StrftimeItems and format_with_items, which is locale-independent and always English. Control run settles it: LC_ALL=C LC_TIME=C, same fixture, same binaries, exit 0, all 11 identical. The fixture is untouched by this branch, so it is red at origin/main on this box too and the red is not this lane's. No gap in compat/tmux-gaps.json records it, so it needs a registry owner; the fix would land in crates/zz-mux, which this cycle's wire rule puts out of reach, so it is measured and left. It is also a limitation of status-row.sh as a baseline: the fixture pins the pane title but not LC_TIME, so its default-row comparison carries the caller's locale; pinning the locale would hide the divergence rather than record it. OTHER PROOFS AT THIS TIP: compat/attached-client.sh exits 0, "attached-client compatibility: PASS". GATE, cycle 1, 2026-09-09 at 5dd932abb93c2e88f3190be42afeeed00ece6368 in /home/demfabris/dev/zz-gate-fixtures: every proof command above re-run at the merged tip on a zz this gate built itself, sha256 ddc5ae0f7be9e52b55dac82a8285c50f74a9684236986d277f54e1d8aa3b3254. Three geometry runs exit 0 at 4.8s, 4.5s and 4.7s, output byte-identical to all six committed runs; attached-client PASS; the backpressure scenario exit 0; tracker_test, both tracker checks and compat/check.sh exit 0. status-row.sh exits 1 exactly as recorded, %b only, and exits 0 under the LC_ALL=C control; the branch touches neither that fixture nor any crate source, so that red is origin/main's on this box and it is retained here as clause 3's fixture limitation. STATUS STAYS ACTIVE: clause 2 is open and cannot be closed on this box, because the recorded timeout happened on macOS and this box is Linux. The proof block recorded here stands for CLAUSES 1 AND 3 ONLY and is not a claim about clause 2. The reviewer's one confirmed defect was a nit addressed to the gate rather than to the branch - record the hash of the zz the gate builds, not environment.txt's 3cb6e284 - and it is done: ddc5ae0f7be9e52b55dac82a8285c50f74a9684236986d277f54e1d8aa3b3254 is a fourth distinct hash for source identical to origin/main, which settles that a debug build of zz is not reproducible here and that provenance rests on reproduction. SPLIT 2026-09-09: fabrico deferred the macOS reproduction (no macbook access now; the campaign continues on Linux) and the macOS half of clause 2 moved to TUI-013, added scope, so the baseline number never counts it as quietly done. What this obligation claims under the amended clause 2 is exactly what its proof block already records: the fixture retains the full timeout dump, proven by sabotage (fourteen files under timeout-diagnostics/), and the recorded macOS expiry is neither reproduced nor explained HERE - that work is TUI-013's, opening on this attempt's refutation of the stale-binary story and the retention machinery. decided 2026-09-09 by fabrico, relayed in-session to the orchestrator ('can we continue for now and record that test for later'); reversible - reopening TUI-001 and folding TUI-013 back undoes it.

items.title: Complete screen and interaction comparison
acceptance: Reuse existing attached-client drivers to compare all decoded cells, glyph widths, styles, cursor position/visibility/shape, geometry and resulting interaction state at named settled checkpoints.
Demonstrate that independent glyph, color/attribute, cursor and geometry changes fail with a useful location/state difference. Equivalent raw escape spellings must not fail.

Retain captures and environment at 80, 100, 109 and 120 columns, including small heights, split/zoom/resize and status off/on/multiple rows/top/bottom. Declare each controlled dynamic value and comparison rule.
items.evidence_note: MEASURED 2026-09-09 on alienware by the new fixture compat/tui-screen-diff.sh, which compares EVERY decoded cell of both screens plus the cursor at named settled checkpoints, both binaries attached inside one outer pinned tmux. zz sha256 3cb6e28437cd028b49c2c2eb07c4414a69226518bf2f287e7c52123d5bf70a38 at 576b6b74; pin d77c9dc6 sha256 df2cafcb212e8b69677dd57c2bd0c3bb59592eaf385d974ec0124526d6b63ee5. RESULT: 33 asserted checkpoints identical, 32 recorded, 65 recorded cursor differences; exit 0 twice in a row, and run 2's 195 capture files are byte-identical to run 1's. Asserted means every row of the outer pane matched byte for byte with its escapes and the asserted cursor tuple matched, at 80x24, 100x24 and 80x10, across fresh attach, status off, status on, split-window -v, resize-pane -Z, unzoom, an outer resize away and back, status 2, status-position top, and a row of CJK, combining and emoji glyphs. Not one cell differed. Two results beyond the count: the small height 80x10 behaves exactly like the wide sizes, and resizing the 120-column client down to 100 makes the two screens identical again cell for cell, so the sidebar is the whole of the 109-and-above difference and hiding it leaves nothing behind. CLAUSE 2, the demonstration: --self-check exits 0 only when four sabotages are each caught in their own channel and three equivalences are reported nowhere. glyph (one character of OUTPUT, from a file each side reads under its own HOME so the typed command is identical bytes) -> rows differ; colour (status-style bg=red on one side) -> rows differ; cursor (an unterminated line of a different length) -> the CURSOR tuple differs; geometry (split-window on one side) -> rows differ; and attribute order in a style, bg=red against bg=colour1, and \033[1mBOLD\033[0m against \033[01mBOLD\033[m -> nothing differs. Two of these were rebuilt after the first attempt measured something other than what it claimed. colour.c colour_fromstring gives red the value 1 and colour1 the value 1|COLOUR_FLAG_256, two DIFFERENT values, and yet both reach the outer grid as the same cell and capture-pane -e re-emits both as \e[41m, so the pair really does collapse: the fixture states the measurement, not the header-file reading. The first cursor sabotage sent a marker afterwards, which put the cursor back at a fresh prompt on both sides and reported no cursor difference at all; it now settles on a substring the two sides' own sabotage output share. CLAUSE 3, the covered subset: 80, 100, 109 and 120 columns, a small height at 80x10, split, zoom and resize, and status off, on, two rows, top and bottom are all driven, with all 195 captures and both cursor tuples retained. Every controlled dynamic value is declared in the fixture header with its rule: status-right '' (the clock, and the %d-%b-%y locale divergence TUI-001 recorded), status-left L, automatic-rename off plus rename-window win, select-pane -T (the recorded pane.runtime-facts decision), and an inner shell of ENV= PS1='$ ' exec /bin/sh handed to new-session and split-window. Global options are reset to each server's defaults before every attach so a case cannot leak into the next. WHAT REMAINS, and the one judgement the reviewer should make: all three clauses have evidence on this branch, so this is review, but ONE channel is compared and printed without being gated. Clause 1 asks for the cursor's SHAPE to be COMPARED and it is, on both sides at all 65 checkpoints, with both values printed every run; it is not asserted, because zz and the pin genuinely differ there today, and a sabotage of that channel could not be told apart from the standing divergence. A shape regression would therefore not turn this fixture red. If the reviewer reads clause 1 as requiring a gate rather than a comparison, downgrade this to active on that point alone; nothing else in the three clauses is short. THREE NEW DIVERGENCES, none with a registry owner, all recorded with both sides' bytes printed on every run. (a) CURSOR ATTRIBUTES, at 65 of 65 checkpoints: the pin reports shape=default blinking=0 colour=none and zz reports shape=block blinking=1 colour=#e5c07b, because crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs:1770-1799 writes DECSCUSR and an OSC 12 cursor colour on every cursor placement while the pin writes neither. Cursor position and visibility ARE asserted and match everywhere. (b) COLOUR CLASSES in the pane body: the same three cells written as named, indexed and RGB come back from the pin as \e[31m, \e[38;5;196m and \e[38;2;1;2;3m, and from zz as \e[38;2;205;0;0m, \e[38;2;255;0;0m and \e[38;2;1;2;3m. zz resolves the named and the indexed cell through its palette and hands the terminal RGB. tui.status-row's closed class-1 finding fixed the STATUS ROW; the pane body still promotes. (c) DEFAULT FOREGROUND: with status-style bg=colour4 and no foreground named, the pin emits no foreground and zz emits an explicit RGB 216,222,233. Under the default status-style the two agree byte for byte, which is why compat/status-row.sh never saw it. None of the three is fixable inside this cycle's zones: (a) is in crates/zz-tui/src outside TUI-001's excursion, and (b) and (c) reach the daemon's frame representation. Also not covered by this attempt: mouse, focus and bracketed paste (TUI-008), copy mode and search overlays (TUI-005), pane-border-status (TUI-004), more than one window, and a second attached client. THE SETTLE, measured not assumed: the marker alone was not enough. Two runs disagreed at the 80x24 zoom checkpoint, zz row 11 holding '$' in one and nothing in the next, because the shell writes the marker line and the prompt that follows it as two separate writes and a capture can land between them. A checkpoint is now settled when its marker is on the screen AND the screen has not changed between two polls; three consecutive runs after that fix were exit 0 with byte-identical captures. No wait in the fixture is a sleep. The timeout dump earned its place before it was sabotaged: the first full run timed out at 109x24 and the retained screen showed in one line that zz draws its sidebar to the LEFT of the pane there, so the marker shared its row with sidebar cells and a whole-line match could never succeed - a fixture fault, fixed by matching the marker as a substring. GATE, cycle 1, 2026-09-09 at 5dd932abb93c2e88f3190be42afeeed00ece6368: all three clauses re-proved at the merged tip on a zz this gate built itself, sha256 ddc5ae0f7be9e52b55dac82a8285c50f74a9684236986d277f54e1d8aa3b3254 - a THIRD independent binary after the worker's and the reviewer's. tui-screen-diff.sh exit 0 in 57.3s with the same summary line, and its 195 capture files plus its 29242-byte stdout are byte-identical to the committed evidence (diff -r exit 0, zero bytes); --self-check exit 0 in 24.1s with stdout byte-identical to the committed self-check.stdout.txt; attached-client PASS; both trackers and compat/check.sh exit 0. Nothing any fixture reported contradicts this obligation. STATUS STAYS REVIEW RATHER THAN VERIFIED, and the reason is the ledger's own rule, not a doubt about the evidence: compat/tui/tracker.py requires every dependency of a verified obligation to be verified too, and this obligation depends on TUI-001, which stays active on its open clause 2, so setting verified here would make tracker.py check fail. The proof block is recorded anyway: the cycle that closes TUI-001 clause 2 on macOS can flip this to verified on these measurements without re-running them. The reviewer confirmed no defect on this obligation. VERIFIED 2026-09-09: TUI-001 reached verified when its macOS clause split to TUI-013 (fabrico's deferral, recorded there), which satisfies the dependency rule; per this note's own provision the banked, thrice-reproduced measurements flip this obligation without re-running them. No new measurement was taken for this flip.
items.next_action: Done. The three recorded divergences still need registry owners (cursor attributes from crates/zz-tui/src/render.rs:1770-1799, named and indexed colours promoted to RGB in the pane body, and the explicit default foreground); the recorded half of the cursor tuple starts asserting the moment the first of those closes. items.title: Stock launcher, command and key behavior
acceptance: With clean config roots, compare bare packaged launch, attach and new-session on empty/live servers plus new-window and split-window. Assert stdout/stderr/exits, selected targets, pane kinds and the complete attached screen.
Drive unmodified stock split, chooser, rename, selection, zoom and detach bindings through actual stdin. Direct split-window creating a terminal does not substitute for testing its stock binding.

Test root bindings and application keys overlapping Ctrl-\ and Alt-s/Alt-S. Chrome cannot consume them outside its owning context. Exercise explicit config roots, -f and existing zz layering separately and record any policy conflict.
items.evidence_note: Measured on this box against pinned d77c9dc6 with two new differential fixtures, both driven inside one outer pinned tmux and both carrying a --self-check that sabotages every channel they compare. CLAUSE 1, compat/tui-launch-diff.sh, 29 comparisons at 80x24 (stdout+stderr+exit as one string, server facts, every decoded screen cell, the cursor tuple): attach-session on an empty server, attach-session -t <missing> on a live one, new-session -d twice, new-session -A -d, new-window -d, split-window -d and both against a missing target, all byte-identical to the pin; attach-session -t and a bare new-session both paint a screen identical to the pin's, cursor included. Two launcher behaviours are recorded, not asserted, because they are recorded decisions this obligation does not own: the bare launcher on a live server (zz runs new-session -A and attaches to `existing` where the pin makes a second session named `1`, semantic:bare-launcher-attach-current), and the bare launcher's screen (measured 2026-09-09 on Linux: `zz` with no arguments starts the native desktop client, which attaches to the daemon and leaves the terminal to its own output, while `tmux` with no arguments paints a session in the terminal it was run from; both leave exactly one attached session, which the case asserts). CLAUSE 1 FIX: the raw-terminal client wrote its log records onto the terminal it was about to paint. Two defects, both in crates/zz/src/diagnostics/mod.rs: process_role matched the literal argument `attach`, so `attach-session` and `new-session` (every spelling a user or a packaged client actually types) fell through to the `command` role and logged to stderr; and RingLogWriter mirrored every record to stderr whenever stderr was a terminal, so even the `tui` role wrote over the screen. Before the fix a `zz new-session -s fresh` left seven rows of `level=INFO role=tui ... process_start` on row 0 (launch-log-noise.before-fix.txt); after it the terminal carries zero log records on both sides, which is the launch-scrollback case. CLAUSE 2, compat/tui-stock-keys.sh, 50 cases at 80x24 and 100x24: every stock chord is typed into the ATTACHED CLIENT'S STDIN with send-keys against the OUTER pane, never executed as a command, and each case waits on a bounded observable, settles, then compares the whole screen, the cursor and a server-facts line. Measured before the fix: prefix % and prefix " ran the zz-native `split-picker` and opened a Picker pane where the pin opens a shell, and prefix s and prefix w ran `focus-sidebar` and moved focus into zz's own sidebar where the pin opens a session or window tree. ITEM 1, WINDOW SIZING UNDER STATUS ROWS: options.c options_push_changes runs recalculate_sizes after every option write and resize.c clients_calculate_size sizes a window at the client's tty rows minus status_line_size, so the pin resizes every window of a session when the status block grows; zz back-solved the extent from the active pane's reported geometry alone and the active pane keeps its height, so at 80x10 with a split the pin's window was 8 rows (%0 h=3, %1 h=4) and zz's stayed 9 (%0 h=4, %1 h=4). zz-mux set_status_option now emits StatusRowsChanged whenever a write moves StatusFormats::rows, and the daemon resizes every window of the affected sessions from its attached clients through MuxEngine::resize_window_to_extent, which leaves window-size alone and skips a manual window the way the pin's clients_calculate_size does. What holds the new extent against the client's next report is that the daemon pushes the new pane geometries as DeferredTerminalCommand::Resize in the same effect drain, so the report the client sends back already carries the new size and back-solves to the extent the window now has; the last_extent_probe the resize clears is a skip filter, not a suppressor, and clearing it makes an identical repeat report processable rather than blocked (set_pane_geometry's 'probe: block breaks out false when the probe matches). Re-probed on both binaries over the fixture's exact sequence at 80x10, 80x6 and 80x24: every window extent and every pane height agrees, the round trip back to `status on` included (attempt-05/pin-and-zz-status-sizing.txt). A zz-daemon unit test drives status 2 on a split window at 80x10 and asserts the pin's 8 rows with 3 beside 4, then the pin's 9 with 4 beside 4 on the way back. ITEM 2, STYLED-LEFT-TRIM: format-draw.c's trims walk format_width's units, so a #[...] section is copied through at no cost to the limit, a run of #s costs the columns it draws escaped and a wide character costs two; zz's truncate_value counted every printable byte, so #{T;=/#{status-left-length}:status-left} answered '#[fg=red,b' where the pin answered '#[fg=red,bold]LEFT' and the unterminated marker took the whole band off the row. The trim now walks the same units styled_display_width already walked, left and right. Probed on both binaries over 72 answers, six values covering escaped hashes, a style after them, wide characters and an unterminated section against twelve modifiers with and without a marker: 72 agree, 0 differ (attempt-05/pin-and-zz-styled-trim.txt), and 27 of them are pinned as a zz-mux unit test. items.evidence_note: ATTEMPT-03, CYCLE 9. EVERY CLAUSE ASSERTS AND THE FIXTURE RECORDS NOTHING. compat/tui-choosers.sh ends `all 78 asserted comparisons identical, 0 recorded not asserted (0 for a sibling lane)` on each of three runs at this tip, exit 0, and its --self-check ends `self-check complete: every sabotage was caught and both equivalences passed` with twelve sabotages, two of them new here. THE THREE CASES THE CYCLE 6 AND CYCLE 8 GATES LEFT, all in clause 2, are `same`. (1) and (2) output-search-prompt and output-search-typed. Both stock search bindings are `command-prompt -P` (key-bindings.c:569-570 and 654), and -P is window_pane_set_prompt, so the prompt hangs on the pane the command targeted rather than on the client and redraw_draw_pane_prompt (screen-redraw.c:1524) draws it over that pane's LAST row - its first under status-position top - leaving status_redraw the status row. CommandPromptState gains a trailing `pane: Option<PaneId>` (v102, pure append, the raw TUI is the consumer half and shipped in the same push), the mux fills it from -P with the invocation's own pane, and the raw TUI paints that row in message-style over the pane's own default cells and puts the cursor on it. `-P` with no pane to resolve raises nothing, which is cmd_command_prompt_exec's early CMD_RETURN_NORMAL. Measured at this tip at 80x24: both sides carry `(search down) ` on row 22 with the status row kept and the cursor at 14,22, where before the pin was on row 22 and zz on row 23. (3) output-selected. window_copy_command clears data->searchmark for every command that is not search-* unless the clear column says never (window-copy.c:3767); zz already carried the rule as CopyModeAction::clears_search_marks, but copy_mode_snapshot pushed its match overlays from the view's own search rather than from the marks, so begin-selection plus cursor-right left the current match painted under the selection in the retained command output. The overlays follow the marks now and the pin's plain `77` is what both sides paint. THE REGRESSION GATE THE BATCH NAMED IS GREEN: compat/tui-copy-mode.sh ends `all 147 cases agree on every channel they assert, 0 recorded a difference elsewhere` with its --self-check clean, so TUI-005 stands. items.title: Mouse, paste, focus and key ownership
acceptance: Compare stock/custom root and copy mouse bindings, drag selection, border resize, status clicks, wheel and double/triple clicks with mouse on/off and application tracking.

items.evidence_note: Cycle 9, the mouse lane, alienware and then the ubuntu box for the fix pass after the review's REJECT, against pinned tmux d77c9dc6; evidence at compat/tui/evidence/TUI-008/attempt-03, whose notes.md carries this obligation's history and the fix pass's own section, history in attempt-02 and attempt-01. WHAT ASSERTS NOW. compat/tui-mouse.sh's own summary line at this tip is "35 asserted checks, 3 recorded checks" followed by "all 35 asserted checks identical", over three runs byte-identical at md5 76e3cc87, and a fourth at the ledger commit itself with the same md5, where the cycle-8 gate left 26 asserted and 10 recorded and the rejected tip left 33 and 3. Its --self-check drives three quiet controls and nineteen one-sided sabotages with every one caught in its own channel. NINE CHECKS HAVE MOVED FROM RECORDED TO ASSERTED, in four channels: the wheel over a pane (2), the drag that selects (3), the click sequence (2) and, this fix pass, the two new cases that drive a pointer at a pane WITH APPLICATION TRACKING ARMED (2). WHAT CLAUSE 1 IS MEASURED ON, exactly, because an earlier draft of this note claimed more than the fixture could see. Under \033[?1002h\033[?1006h the fixture now drives a press, a motion with the button held and the release that ends the drag (app-mouse-drag/reports), and two clicks inside the click timeout (app-mouse-double-click/reports), and asserts the reports the pane's own program printed, in order: \e[<0;2;3M \e[<32;8;3M \e[<0;8;3m and \e[<0;5;3M \e[<0;5;3m \e[<0;5;3M \e[<0;5;3m, identical on both binaries. Under \033[?1000h it drives a single click on both sides with mouse on and with mouse off (app-mouse-mouse-on, app-mouse-mouse-off). It does NOT drive a triple click or a wheel with tracking armed; case_drag_selects, case_multi_click, case_wheel_up_pane and case_wheel_up_alternate all run with no application mouse, which is the other half of clause 1 and is where the wheel, the drag and the click sequence assert. THE REVIEW'S THREE FINDINGS AND WHAT EACH COST. (1) THE WIRE: the branch appended view_action and press_action to InputMessage::MouseKey while PROTOCOL_VERSION stayed at 102, which shipped in zz 0.9.0 and 0.9.1. PROTOCOL_VERSION is 103 now, the two appends have a v103 entry of their own in knowledge/protocol/wire-protocol.md's version history with the lines moved out of v102, and three assertions moved with it rather than two: crates/zz-protocol/src/message.rs, the assertion at crates/zz-protocol/tests/hunt_claims.rs:18 whose test name carried the number, and the byte-for-byte hello frame in the same file, which carries the version twice. compat/wire-version.py, read out of origin/main because this branch's base predates it, exits 0 at this tip. (2) and (3) A DRAG LOST ITS RELEASE and A DOUBLE CLICK REPORTED OUT OF ORDER, one hole with one fix: server_client_handle_key ends a mouse key that matched nothing at forward_key, where window_pane_key re-encodes the event for the pane, and the daemon consumed it instead. Measured at 142139fd against the pin: the drag's pane printed \e[<0;2;3M \e[<32;8;3M and not the release, because MouseDragEnd1Pane is installed in the two copy tables and in no root table; the double click's pane printed press, release, release, press, because SecondClick1Pane is bound nowhere in root either and the client swallowed it until the 300 ms timer delivered it through DoubleClick1Pane's send -M. THE FIX, three hunks: crates/zz-daemon/src/daemon.rs input_mouse_key forwards the event's own pane input when no binding matched and root was the first table tried (the pin's first != table guard), and forwards only a TerminalViewAction::Mouse because input_key_mouse writes only while ALL_MOUSE_MODES is set; crates/zz-tui/src/input.rs stops swallowing a click-sequence name nothing is bound to and lets the daemon decide; crates/zz-mux/src/command.rs send-keys -M writes nothing when the invoking key is a DoubleClick name, which is m->ignore (server-client.c:838,908 and input-keys.c:805) and is why the pin's pane sees four reports and not five, while window_copy_command's own cursor move reads m regardless of ignore (window-copy.c:3725) so the copy-mode half of the same binding is untouched. PRODUCT DECISIONS, two, each with the old behaviour and the pin's measured one. (1) THE PIN'S PANE-BODY AND COPY-TABLE MOUSE ROWS RUN THE PIN'S COMMANDS, AND A MOUSE KEY NOTHING CLAIMED REACHES THE PANE: a wheel, a drag, a middle click and a click sequence over a pane used to run the raw TUI's own pointer code, list-keys answered 5 root rows against the pin's 27 and 0 mouse rows in either copy table against the pin's 7 each, and a mouse key the daemon found no binding for was dropped; key-bindings.c:498-522 and :592-598 install those rows as ordinary binds and server-client.c:1557-1571 hands an unmatched one to the pane. Eleven of the twenty-seven root rows and all fourteen copy-table rows are installed now, a config that unbinds or rebinds one changes what the gesture does on the raw TUI exactly as it does on the pin, the raw TUI's own wheel scrolling, drag selection and double-click word selection are gone for those gestures, and a release, a second press or any other name the root table does not bind reaches the pane the event landed on while that pane tracks. Measured: the nine checks above. Decided 2026-09-14 by the orchestrator under fabrico's TUI parity contract of 2026-09-09; reversible. The GUI is untouched: it sends no mouse key. (2) select-word LEAVES THE EMACS CURSOR ONE CELL PAST THE WORD: it used to stop on the word's last cell under both mode-keys, and with the emacs end exclusive the copy dropped that cell; window_copy_cursor_next_word_end backs the cursor up one only under vi. Measured on the pin with mode-keys emacs and 'alpha beta gamma': a select-word at column 7 leaves the cursor at 10 and copies beta, where zz left it at 9 and copied bet. This reaches every client, including the GUI, and it is a fix in the pin's direction. Decided 2026-09-14 by the orchestrator under fabrico's TUI parity contract of 2026-09-09; reversible. GAPS: twenty-two items closed by the first pass, each with a dated 2026-09-14 measurement; the fix pass closes none and reopens none. keys.root-native-mouse closes six of its twenty-two (MouseDown1Pane, MouseDown2Pane, MouseDrag1Pane, WheelUpPane, DoubleClick1Pane, TripleClick1Pane) and keeps sixteen; keys.copy-mode-native-mouse closes all fourteen and moves to the closed list; mouse.bound-context closes flag:send-keys:-M and keeps flag:copy-mode:-S and flag:move-pane:-M; formats.mouse-context keeps all five, because mouse_line, mouse_word and mouse_hyperlink need the screen under the pointer and mouse_status_line and mouse_status_range the status range, and no command reads either yet; formats.terminal-runtime, not one of this batch's four gaps, closes format:mouse_any_flag because compat_manifest_tests refuses a tracked item for a format zz answers. Each accepted gap keeps its decision for the GUI and for every item not closed. WHAT REMAINS, three recorded checks, two of them measured divergences and the third a hold over a channel that currently agrees, none of them a sibling of an earlier lane and all of them TUI-008's own. right-click-pane and status-clicks/right-click-screen (2): both are display-menu -t= -x M -y M over DEFAULT_PANE_MENU's twenty-eight items and DEFAULT_WINDOW_MENU's eleven; -x M and -y M answer the screen centre on the raw TUI rather than the event's cell and the status range it landed in, and the pane menu additionally reads mouse_word, mouse_line and mouse_hyperlink, which formats.mouse-context still holds. paste-under-menu/screen (1) IS NOT A MEASURED DIVERGENCE: on this box at this tip the two screens agree, all 24 rows identical on seven of seven runs - the fix pass's four evidence files and the review's three - with paste-under-menu/option alpha on both and the menu genuinely raised on both sides before the paste is sent, since case_paste_under_menu binds prefix-E to display-menu and both_screen_has PASTEMENU waits for it on each side. An earlier draft of this note stated as present fact that the pin's overlay eats the paste-start key and leaves a trailing ~ where the raw TUI hands the tail over as a fresh bracketed paste; it does not reproduce and that claim is withdrawn. The channel is held at record, and only at record, until a lane drives it one-sided with a --self-check sabotage and flips it to same; what keeps it worth a driver rather than a blind assert is that the two binaries reach the tail of a bracketed paste by different routes - the pin takes the run key by key through the overlay where the raw TUI turns the whole run into one Paste event before any overlay sees it (crates/zz-tui/src/input.rs handle_paste, crates/zz-client/src/menu.rs resolve_menu_paste) - so a different payload or a different menu could still separate them. ZONE EXCURSIONS: crates/zz-terminal/src/interaction.rs for a trailing CopyModeAction::MouseCursor, forced by the measurement that every existing pointer action in copy mode resets the selection where window_copy_move_mouse only moves the cursor; crates/zz-daemon/src/status.rs for one match arm; and the partition counts in compat_manifest_tests.rs with the one hunt_claims.rs claim that asserted send-keys -M unsupported, all moved in the same commits. The fix pass took no new excursion. STATUS: active. Three checks still record, so verified would be a lie. PROOFS AT THIS TIP, all on the ubuntu box, all exit 0: tui-mouse 35 asserted and 3 recorded, three runs byte-identical at md5 76e3cc87, plus its self-check with nineteen sabotages caught; tui-stock-keys 50 cases agreeing, with eight or nine recorded elsewhere depending on load, plus its self-check; the count wobbles because application-reader's documented pane_current_command timing record is raised at 80x24 and, under load, again at 100x24, a channel attempt-03 had as ok and which no hunk of this pass can reach; attached-client PASS; tui-copy-mode 147 with none recorded; tui-caps 366 asserted rows with none recorded, which is the fixture that asserts #{mouse_any_flag} on both sides; 53 rows of the delta corpus for send-keys, copy-mode and list-keys - its 21 non-smoke rows, the 30 smoke rows whose text names send-keys, send -, copy-mode, list-keys, bind-key, bind -, Mouse, Wheel, Click, select-word or paste-buffer, and copy-mode-stock-action-keys and command-prompt-editing, the two slow rows closest to this pass - every channel clean on every row; the rest of that 167-scenario selection is the smoke set, run whole by the first pass and named in 10-corpus-delta.txt, and no hunk of this pass can reach a corpus row at all, because input_mouse_key runs only for InputMessage::MouseKey, which only a client with a pointer sends, and the send-keys -M gate needs an invoking key named DoubleClick, which only the click timer produces; cargo test over zz-protocol, zz-mux, zz-tui, zz-daemon and zz (125 cli_binary tests included), clippy with -D warnings over zz-protocol, zz-mux, zz-tui and zz-daemon, cargo fmt --check over the four, compat/wire-version.py and compat/check.sh, which runs compat/tui/verify-claims.py ("every verified obligation holds up"). GATED onto main at 3ecd4702 on the ubuntu box, where compat/tui-mouse.sh reported "35 asserted checks, 3 recorded checks" and "all 35 asserted checks identical" on three runs byte-identical at md5 76e3cc87, and the gate's review record sits beside this note at compat/tui/evidence/TUI-008/attempt-03/review.md.

items.evidence_note: Cycle 8, the caps lane, alienware, against pinned tmux d77c9dc6; evidence at compat/tui/evidence/TUI-009/attempt-05 (attempt-01 to attempt-04 are read-only history, and attempt-04/notes.md carries cycle 7's mouse work, its review and the punch list this attempt closes). EVERY CLAUSE ASSERTS. compat/tui-caps.sh asserts 366 rows and records NONE, from 351 and 15 at origin/main; three runs byte-identical at md5 cb21624a, and its --self-check catches 27 one-sided sabotages with 6 controls quiet, from 24 and 5. All fifteen rows attempt-04 left recorded closed, in the three causes it named. CLAUSE 2, THIRTEEN ROWS, THE CAPABILITY WIRE: client_colours and client_termfeatures on facts/bare, facts/-2, facts/-u, facts/-T and facts/utf8-locale, and client_termfeatures on silent/bare, silent/-T and silent/-2. items.title: Slow output, recovery and client lifecycle
acceptance: Measure prolonged terminal backpressure past the writer budget, deliver an observable bound key while undrained, and verify bounded memory and response within a declared reference-derived deadline.
Resume reading and compare the final screen. Detach under backlog and prove no queued paint appears after terminal restoration.
Exercise different-sized simultaneous terminal clients, read-only attach, detach/reattach and supported transport recovery. Compare selected targets, geometry, focus and final screen.
items.evidence_note: All three clauses measured and proved on this box (alienware, CachyOS, 16 cores) on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10. CLAUSE 1, MEASURED FIRST with compat/tui-output-backpressure.sh, whose relay (compat/tui-output-relay.py) is a pty in an outer pinned tmux pane that stops reading on command while keys keep flowing, at 80x24 with the registry's 45 s undrained window and a bound F5. BEFORE, at origin/main bfd05821: pinned tmux d77c9dc6 answered in 0.033 s and grew 0 kB over the window from a 4892 kB baseline; zz did not answer within the 12 s the registry recorded and grew 6144 kB from a 105956 kB baseline. AFTER: zz answers in 0.025 s and grows 6572 kB. Memory was bounded on both sides before and after, so the 4 MiB budget was never what cost the client its liveness and the budget did not move; what changed is the behaviour past it. crates/zz-tui/src/writer.rs now drops the whole queue the way tty.c tty_block_maybe drains its out buffer, keeps dropping for the pin's 100 ms TTY_BLOCK_INTERVAL, and clears the block on the first interval that dropped less than BLOCK_STOP, keeping the pin's 64:1 START:STOP ratio against a whole-paint queue. Clearing it repaints from the model the way tty_timer_callback sets CLIENT_ALLREDRAWFLAGS and calls tty_invalidate: render.rs throws away its painted state on a drop and app.rs takes a MainEvent::Repaint from the writer's block timer. Control bytes a dropped paint carried go back to the front of the next paint, because a mode change is not something a repaint reproduces. The declared response deadline is 1.000 s, twenty times the 0.050 s the registry recorded for the pin, and the pin runs as a side of the fixture so every run proves the deadline is achievable here. CLAUSE 2: after the relay resumes, the recovered screen is identical to the pin cell for cell above the status row with the same cursor tuple, and after a detach taken while undrained zz wrote 40 bytes and ZERO escape bytes after leaving the alternate screen. CLAUSE 3, in compat/attached-client.sh (--lifecycle runs the three new probes alone): different-sized simultaneous clients at 90x20 and 70x30 under every window-size rule, which corrected the premise that the pin sizes to the smallest - options-table.c defaults window-size to WINDOW_SIZE_LATEST, so the untouched default follows the most recently used client (70x30 then 90x20 as each is used) and only an explicit smallest takes the componentwise 70x20, largest the componentwise 90x30, with both clients keeping their own geometry throughout; read-only attach proved in all four of the pin's parts, typing that never reaches the pane, a bound run-shell that never runs, a bound switch-client that does, and a live screen, with the refusals proved in order against a bound key pressed by the read-write client rather than by a sleep; and three detach/reattach cycles alternating a client-key detach with a server-side detach-client against the tty, each one asserting the selected target, the client geometry, the focus flag and the marker still on the screen. Supported transport recovery measured beyond that: with the real daemon killed (the zz daemon forks, so the pid that owns the socket is the child), both binaries print [server exited unexpectedly] and exit 1, the pin within 0.05 s and zz within 0.1 s. Every added case sabotaged once and caught in its own assertion, and the whole fixture goes red against a build from before the drop path. RECORDED, not asserted: the cursor shape/blink/colour divergence (canvas lane owns it); the status row's explicit default foreground, byte for byte the same before this change and after it; and that the pin's client never leaves an alternate screen at all, so its escape tail has no restoration point to be after. tui.client-output-queue-budget is closed on this proof. GATE 2026-09-10: the review's second nit is recorded rather than fixed, because fixing it is a behaviour change that would need this fixture re-proved against a new timing claim, which is a lane's work. Measured and confirmed at the gate: tmux tty.c tty_block_maybe zeroes tty->discarded when it starts a block (tty.c:241), so the pin's first 100 ms interval counts only bytes offered after the drop and its block can end after one interval, while crates/zz-tui/src/writer.rs submit sets discarded = queued + bytes.len(), folding the whole dropped queue into the first interval; BLOCK_STOP is QUEUE_BUDGET/64, so the first tick always continues and a zz block lasts at least two intervals. The 64:1 START:STOP ratio claim is exact; the block START rule is not the pin's, and this sentence exists so a later reader does not take it for the pin's. Bounded, and input stays live throughout. The lane also rewrote its own record's sources array, which is a field a worker may not write; the gate kept the corrected array because the reviewer verified it against the diff and it is factually right.

It wants a line-fact channel out of the terminal worker, not a sixth text transform. -H prints each line's OSC 8 URIs and there is no hyperlink in zz's snapshot to print: measured on the row the pin marks HX, the pin's -e emits ^[]8;id=zzid;https://example.com/a^[\LINK^[]8;;^[\ and zz's emits LINK. -P prints input_pending(wp->ictx) and libghostty-vt publishes no parser-pending buffer; an empty answer would be a fake channel that matched only because that buffer is almost always empty. -R IS THE ONE THAT WAS WEIGHED: it dumps the pin's internal grid, a header G <sx>x<sy> (<hsize>/<hlimit>), then per line L <yy> (<n>) flags=<string>[<hex>] <cellused>/<cellsize>, then one C line per column with that cell's colour, attribute and link ids - measured at 40x8, 329 lines for eight rows. zz has no hsize/hlimit pair, no per-line cellused and cellsize and no grid flag word, and building them inside zz would be inventing tmux internals so that bytes match. The workload it would serve is a tmux regression test reading another tmux's grid. Decided 2026-09-15 by the orchestrator under fabrico's TUI parity contract of 2026-09-09; reversible. The gap stays accepted for -F, -H, -P, -R and the two semantic items. A SECOND MEASUREMENT FOR CLAUSE 2, beyond the one trailing cell it names: on a coloured row the pin's -e writes ^[[31mRED^[[39m and zz writes ^[[0m^[[38;5;1mRED^[[0m, so the colour spelling and the reset differ too. The fixture's scene has no colour, which is why the roster only ever saw the trailing cell. That also holds -C -e open here: the combination is implemented and correct as a transform and can only match once -e matches.
